title: Hyundai Is Now Officially Training Humanoid Robots for Factory Jobs at Metaplant America
source_used: economy.ac and Manufacturing Dive (autoevolution, the item's outlet, returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Boston Dynamics, owned by Hyundai, opened the Robotics Metaplant Application Center (RMAC) at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America near Savannah, Georgia, in September 2026 (economy.ac, Manufacturing Dive).
Manufacturing Dive says robot training there began on a pilot basis in June.
Atlas is being trained first on parts sequencing, which means picking and arranging components in assembly order.
Boston Dynamics plans to expand Atlas to machine tending and assembling kits for individual orders.
Hyundai plans to introduce Atlas into real production operations from 2028 and component assembly in 2030 (economy.ac).
Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas units across Kia and other plants (Manufacturing Dive).
The autoevolution report of 8 Oct could not be read; this entry rests on the two other outlets.
quote_evidence: Boston Dynamics also opened the Robotics Metaplant Application Center (RMAC) at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America (HMGMA), near Savannah, Georgia, last month and began training its Atlas humanoid for manufacturing processes.
Hyundai Motor Group likewise plans to introduce Atlas into actual production operations from 2028, before extending its use to component assembly processes in 2030.
It began training its robots for repetitive tasks at the Robotics Metaplant Application Center on a pilot basis in June.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows Atlas still training, not yet working on a real production line.
event_date: RMAC opened Sep 2026; pilot training from Jun 2026
